doc.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995

title: Goodman hearing Jimmy Noone and Johnny Dodds in Chicago
summary: Williams says Goodman's playing came out of Noone and the Dodds brothers.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: And when he puts that instrument in his mouth — now there’s one other thing. You spoke about him in Chicago, Illinois, they used to bring him over to the club to hear Jimmy Noone.
And what were those two brothers, one played drums I think and the other played clarinet. MW: Johnny Dodds?

Johnny Dodds. Thank you, thank you. Johnny Dodds and those cats man, they were something. He came over and when you hear him, if you hear them as you and I did, then you know where Benny came from and where he was. Like “I Know That You Know,” [scats] that stuff he plays all that intricate stuff he plays, man came right out of him, and the lower register things Woody he played.
